tools.why: Enables SVG-to-PNG conversion (WezTerm/kitty can't decode SVG themselves), image-to-PDF export, the redact feature (blacking out rectangles before sharing a screenshot), and the three file operations `:Image scale` / `:Image optimise` / `:Image convert`.

Enables `:Image ocr` — reading the text out of an image (a screenshot of an error message, a scanned page) into a buffer, where it can be searched, copied or translated. Language data beyond English is a separate package per language (tesseract-ocr-deu and friends); `:checkhealth images` lists what is installed. On Windows the UB-Mannheim installer does not add itself to PATH — images.nvim probes the usual install directory anyway, or set `ocr.bin`.
Renders images inline in terminals without a native image protocol (Kitty graphics / iTerm2), as a fallback for the ASCII/terminal preview.
